curated-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-old-h: Expressive and boldly drawn, Autour One keeps each stroke at a cable-like thickness, perfect for a cannabis dispensary logo. Noto Sans Old Hungarian follows with wide-open shapes that stay legible down to tiny sizes, a plain sans that carries paragraphs easily.
curated-gf-averia-gruesa-libre-gf-noto-s: Distinctive Averia Gruesa Libre leads with only light contrast in its strokes. Noto Sans New Tai Lue sits beneath with cupped, rounded letters that are comfortable in small doses, say on fitness app workout cards.
curated-gf-averia-libre-gf-arvo: Arvo reads as a classic serif with curves that refuse to close, dignified and traditional. Averia Libre is the one to show off with, its gently pressed diagonals suiting a headline (maybe a coffee roaster for outdoorsy types), while Arvo is better for brief copy.
curated-gf-averia-libre-gf-gowun-batang: Refined Gowun Batang is the quiet half, cutting its terminals back to leave a big gap. Averia Libre adds a faint but real thick-thin shift up top, so roadmap slides or any short stretch of reading get a commanding start.
curated-gf-averia-sans-libre-fs-amulya: Averia Sans Libre goes bold and plain, with no flourishes to distract. Amulya follows in sans-serif with generous gaps in its curves, so brief copy sized modestly under a much larger heading would suit it well.
curated-gf-averia-serif-libre-gf-ibm-ple: Bold Averia Serif Libre draws a steady line with only faint modulation, and its thicks stay fairly mild up top. Shrink that heading and it loses its punch.
curated-gf-babylonica-gf-noto-sans-indic: Babylonica looks hand-drawn, its strands knitted tight like twisted rope fibers. Noto Sans Indic Siyaq Numbers answers with sweeping open curves that never close up, so the cramped script and the plain sans give each other room.
curated-gf-bad-script-gf-cairo: Bad Script writes like pen on paper, with wide gaps between curve ends and stems, perhaps for a team shirt for event. Cairo is a plain sans with a wide channel into every bowl, and that openness is what the pair does best.
curated-gf-bahianita-fs-azeret-mono: Bahianita tucks its curves like folded wire hooks, every character jammed close together. Azeret Mono spreads out in contrast, with open letter mouths and expansive spacing, and that tight-versus-loose difference is the pair's best trick.
curated-gf-bahianita-gf-suez-one: Expressive Bahianita draws every curve as thick as a straight stem, like a marker. Suez One adds a bookish classic serif with tall-bowled e and a, so the blunt heading and refined text sit comfortably together.
